newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU details Spain's telecoms liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: EU details Spain's telecoms liberalisation.

text.p: The European Commission is set to clear the participation of Telefonica de Espana in the Unisource telecommunications deal in May 1997 following Spain's agreement to liberalise its telecoms market fully by November 30, 1998, Commission sources said.
The sources cited a letter sent last week by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert to the Spanish minister in charge of telecoms, Rafael Arias Salgado.

The letter details a strict timetable for achieving effective competition in the Spanish telecoms sector. The sources said the Commission's offer had been fully accepted by the Spanish government earlier this week in the framework of the WTO talks on global telecoms liberalisation.
Following is the step-by-step opening of Spain's telecoms sector:

- "Immediate authorisation" of the use of so-called alternative telecoms infrastructure operated by utility companies such as railways to provide already liberalised services. The relevant legislation came into force in July, but Spain was resisting its implementation.

- Granting at the beginning of January 1998 a third national telecoms licence to operate basic telephone services. Madrid is expected to give state telecoms firm Retevision a second licence soon which will effectively give it and Telefonica a duopoly until a third operator is allowed.

- Authorisation by the beginning of January 1998 for cable operators to provide basic telephone services. This must include the possibility for such operators to interconnect their respective networks.
- Implementation before the end of July 1998 of all regulations needed for the total opening of the Spanish market to competition.
- Ability for any company to request permission from August 1, 1998 to operate voice telephony network and services.
- The full liberalisation of voice telephone services and infrastructure by November 30, 1998.
The agreement allows for the clearance of Telefonica's 25-percent stake in Unisource, whose other partners are Telia of Sweden, Dutch telecoms operator KPN and the Swiss PTT.
Van Miert said in his letter that the Commission would soon publish a notice saying it intends to clear Telefonica's participation. This would be followed by a formal clearance in May 1997.
